I'm a Ph.D. candidate in physics at Brown University, working on radio interferometry and 21-cm cosmology.

My research focuses on detecting and mitigating radio frequency interference. These (usually) man-made signals corrupt astronomical data, preventing a clean detection of the 21-cm neutral hydrogen line.

frontmatter.title: About Me
interests: Radio interferometry, 21-cm cosmology, and the Epoch of Reionization

node.html:
Hello! I'm Jade Ducharme, a Ph.D. candidate in physics at Brown University, where I work with Prof. Jonathan Pober on radio interferometry and 21-cm cosmology.

I study the Epoch of Reionization – the period in the Universe's history when the first stars and galaxies were forming. The faint 21-cm hydrogen signal from that period is buried under terrestrial radio noise many orders of magnitude brighter, so much of my work is about finding and removing radio frequency interference before it corrupts a cosmological measurement.

My recent work has involved building a Bayesian framework for flagging RFI, modeling moving interference sources (like satellites, or even airplanes), and using interferometric near-field corrections to estimate how high above the array those sources actually are.

I earned my M.Sc. at Brown in 2025 and my B.Sc. in physics at McGill University in 2022. I've been a member of the MWA Collaboration since 2023, and outside research I coordinate and build the site for Astronomy on Tap Rhode Island. I work in French (native) and English (fluent).

• Developing a Bayesian framework for flagging and characterizing radio frequency interference in radio interferometric data, with collaborators at McGill University.
  • Built improved models for moving RFI sources (e.g. satellites and aircraft) and quantified their impact on flagging strategies for Epoch of Reionization analyses, advised by Prof. Jonathan C. Pober.
  • Pioneered altitude estimation of RFI sources using interferometric near-field corrections, published as first author in PASA.
  • Earned an M.Sc. in physics along the way (2025); awarded the Physics Merit Fellowship (2026) and the Forrest Award for experimental apparatus work (2025).

• Member of the Murchison Widefield Array collaboration, contributing to Epoch of Reionization power spectrum analyses.
  • Co-author on MWA collaboration results placing improved limits on the 21 cm signal at z = 6.5–7.0, and on the MWA Phase III instrument upgrade paper.
  • Supported by NSF award #2106510, Collaborative Research: 21 cm Reionization Science with the MWA (2023–2025).
  • Awarded Best Talk at the 2024 MWA Project Meeting.

• Co-supervised undergraduate researchers Neal Frankenberg (Summer 2026) and Jacob Lipman (Spring 2026) at Brown, and Andrei Li (Summer 2025) at McGill.
  • Teaching Assistant for PHYS 0220 (Astronomy, Spring 2023) and PHYS 0270 (Introduction to Astronomy, Fall 2022) at Brown University.

• Coordinate events for the Rhode Island chapter of Astronomy on Tap, bringing astronomy talks to a general public audience.
  • Design, build, and maintain the chapter website at aot-ri.vercel.app.

• Completed a B.Sc. in physics, graduating in 2022.
  • Held an NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award (2021, CAD $7,000).
  • Won the McGill Space Institute Summer Research Showcase Prize (2021).
  • Returned in Summer 2025 to co-supervise an undergraduate researcher and in 2024 for the Precision Calibration Workshop.

frontmatter.title: Improved Modeling for Moving Sources of Radio Frequency Interference

node.html:
Interference from satellites and aircraft moves through the sky during an observation. This work models that motion directly and shows how it changes the flagging (i.e. masking) strategies we should be using.

J. M. Ducharme, J. C. Pober, and M. J. Wilensky.

frontmatter.title: Altitude Estimation of Radio Frequency Interference Sources

node.html:
Using interferometric near-field corrections to work out how high above the array an interfering source actually sits. Localizing an RFI contaminant in three-dimensional space marks an important step towards eventually subtracting it from the data entirely.

J. M. Ducharme & J. C. Pober.

frontmatter.title: The Murchison Widefield Array Phase III Upgrade

node.html:
MWA Phase III upgrade: densitivity doubled, baselines quadrupled, and Epoch of Reionization observations optimised.

S. J. Tingay et al., including J. Ducharme.

frontmatter.title: Improved Limits on the 21 cm Signal at z = 6.5–7.0 Using Gaussian Information

node.html:
Tighter constraints on the 21 cm signal from the Epoch of Reionization, extracting additional Gaussian information from Murchison Widefield Array observations.

C. M. Trott et al., including J. Ducharme.

frontmatter.title: Limits on the 21 cm Power Spectrum at z = 6.5–7.0 from MWA Observations

node.html:
Power spectrum limits on the 21 cm signal during reionization, from deep Murchison Widefield Array integrations.

C. D. Nunhokee et al., including J. Ducharme.
